title: Constantin Turculet(?) to Hetman Sieniawski(?), news from Bender, 1709 (DECODE R7481, R7482)

steps.what: DECODE metadata for R7460-R7507 by API; 130 images of R7462-R7507 with the session cookie; no key or decryption file on any record.

Kaczka, Danubius XXX (2012) prints the Brâncoveanu/Cantacuzino letters of nr 13 and nr 5 from these originals with keys A and B; nothing on the Schenck letters, R7475, R7476, R7481-R7482, R7484-R7485.

Subagents transcribed the unprinted Sieniawski pieces with their interlinear decipherments: R7475 (alphabetical homophonic table rebuilt from the gloss), R7476 and R7484-R7485 (Chomentowski's 3-digit syllabary, syllabary.tsv), R7481-R7482 (key B).
R7481, R7482, R7484, R7485 checked token by token against gloss and key (encipherment slips settled): 99.6%, 100%, 95.9%, 100% read as sense.

Entry split on 14 Oct 2026 from sieniawski1708 under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): the Vienna-Schenck letters are schenck1706; the Sieniawski letters are one entry per key: key A (sieniawski1708), key B (turculet1709), the R7475 table (r7475), the Chomentowski syllabary (chomentowski1713).
Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R7481 and R7482 linked to their token transcriptions, pass-2 checks and readings

Verification 5 (plain bar, 23 Oct 2026): the letter is Polish of 1709 (explicit-hole bar): R7481_reading.txt body explicit 1.0. Rescored with research/reading_audit/v2_score.py; all entries keep read; reading_review notes record both scores.

v6 spelling check (23 Oct 2026, research/reading_audit/v6_spelling_files.txt): R7482_reading.txt ('normalised spelling') put back into the writer's Latin from R7482.txt (figures and interlinear gloss): hæc, quæcunque (the clear &/æ sign), occurunt, expectat, Tarlo, Soczaviæ; no word changed. R7481_reading.txt ('modernised Polish') is not in the v6 list and was not touched. Rescored with research/reading_audit/v2_score.py: R7482_reading.txt plain 0.429 -> 0.318, explicit holes 0.929 -> 0.864. The plain share falls with period spelling against a modern word list; the explicit-hole share, the bar for period spelling, is unchanged or the change comes from the new header lines in files without a '## Reading' heading. No state changes.

R7481 reading restored to the writer's spelling: each word of the 9 Oct modernised Polish re-spelt from the key-B letter stream (K lines of R7481.txt / R7481_pass2.txt), as in research/reading_audit/v6_charalign.py; no word changed, nulls 407/700 kept out, diacritics supplied. R7481 and R7482 translated into English (R7481_en.md, R7482_en.md).

outcome.method_basis: Both letters carry a full contemporary interlinear decipherment (and p. 3 a fair copy of it), transcribed and checked token by token against Kaczka's key B; his edition did not print these letters.
outcome.fraction_read_source: R7481_pass2.txt: 520 of 522 tokens give sense (the two open are the nulls 407, 700); R7482_pass2.txt: 355 of 355; 875 of 877

texts.label: R7481, nr 5 pp. 1-3, Polish news from Bender, 1709
texts.summary: Polish news from Bender for Hetman Sieniawski, probably from Constantin Turculeț in Moldavia, summer 1709: 700 Swedes without arms went with Colonel Gyllenkrook to Suceava, and the King and Mazepa are to go to Rákóczi. Page 3 is a contemporary fair copy of the decipherment.

reading_review.note: Translation wave v9, 23 Oct 2026: R7481_reading.txt restored from the modernised Polish of 9 Oct to the writer's spelling, letter for letter from the key-B figures and the gloss (Ztad, siedmset, Gilenkrukiem, Soczawey, iescze, cztierysta, maley, iusz, tedey, maia, Rakocego, oznaimic, te, Pan Mga), no word changed, Polish diacritics supplied. Body v2_score.py pl: explicit holes 1.0 (9/9), plain 0.111 (the Polish word list does not know 1709 spelling), hole rate 0.0. Rests on the decode, the interlinear gloss and the fair-copy decipherment on p. 3. English in R7481_en.md.

texts.label: R7482, nr 5 pp. 5-6, Latin letter, 1709
texts.summary: A Latin letter on the same news ('Hinc tantum haec occurrunt novalia'), addressed to the Grand Hetman (Sieniawski) and docketed as from the Hospodar of Wallachia: Tarło still waits at Suceava for orders.

prior.where: the contemporary interlinear decipherment; key B printed by Kaczka 2012 fn. 22, the letters not printed
